description: Participants make the cost of language model applications measurable, attributable and smaller without losing quality. For a fictional telecom operator running three applications behind one gateway, a bilingual care assistant, a call-summary job and a billing-dispute agent, they work from a month of synthetic usage traces: they model cost per request and session, attribute spend to teams, set budgets, evaluate model tiers and reasoning settings on their own tasks, route with fallbacks, measure prefix and semantic caches, compare hosted and self-hosted serving and report cost per successful outcome. Cluster capacity planning is AE-307; engine-level optimisation is AE-401.
audience: Practitioners. Engineers who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: a deployed model or language model application they built and can explain.
prerequisites: AE-203 Building Applications on Language Models
AE-205 Deploying AI Services: Containers, Serving and Monitoring
Groups and joins usage logs with SQL or dataframes
Has run an evaluation set against a language model application

outcomes.text: Compute cost per request and per session from prompt, output and cached tokens, retries, agent steps and accelerator-hours, given a month of usage traces and a synthetic invoice
outcomes.evidence: a cost model that reconciles with the invoice within 2%

outcomes.text: Configure attribution, budgets and limits per team, application and environment on a model gateway, given three applications sharing one gateway
outcomes.evidence: a showback table and a replayed spike that trips the hard limit

outcomes.text: Evaluate model tiers, reasoning settings and a routing policy on the operator's own tasks, choosing by cost per successful outcome at a fixed quality floor, given 100 labelled tasks per application
outcomes.evidence: a results table and a router configuration with its measured savings

outcomes.text: Measure how prefix and semantic caching change cost, latency and answer correctness, including isolation between customers, given replayed traffic for the care assistant
outcomes.evidence: hit rates, a wrong-answer rate and a passing cross-customer isolation test

outcomes.text: Decide between hosted APIs and a self-hosted open-weight model with a break-even analysis that includes utilisation and data-placement rules, given price sheets, a throughput benchmark and the operator's classification register
outcomes.evidence: a break-even chart and a recommendation

outcomes.text: Deliver a cost review with three measured savings options to engineering and finance stakeholders, given an unseen capstone scenario
outcomes.evidence: a notebook and a two-page review reporting energy beside cost, defended in ten minutes
